approval_required_for: Any architecture, pipeline, memory layout, runtime ABI, DDR map, numeric policy, or major template change discovered during Stage 8 repair.
Any attempt to reopen a previously passed lower-layer gate without a contradicting boundary trace or CCTG-localized causal slice must be rejected or escalated for explicit backtrack approval.
Ambiguous backend/app-shell target selection, board profile update, or shell integration choice not grounded in cited board materials and real tool evidence.
Any change to golden-reference generation, numeric tolerance policy, or real-weight/input acceptance criteria; smoke/default generated weights must not be substituted for acceptance evidence.
Any planned_tool or planned_checker implementation introduced later because a required real-tool, localization, golden-reference, or board-integration capability is missing.

executable_actions.on_failure: Block Stage 6 promotion, record a stage_retry_request with the failed checker names, and do not hand off to Stage 7 until the final artifacts are repaired and rechecked.
executable_actions.rationale: Aggregate the specialist sub-DAG summaries into checker-verifiable Stage 6 handoff artifacts while preserving the distinction between current-stage plan/contract pass and downstream real-tool execution.

executable_actions.on_failure: Treat the failure as an artifact/checker/golden-reference materialization issue; block all functional acceptance runs and return a bounded Stage 6 retry or Stage 8 checker-repair request with the failed artifact names.
executable_actions.rationale: Real input/weight manifests, DDR images, boundary contracts, and reproducible testbench scaffolds are prerequisite artifacts for non-smoke functional verification and repair-localization traces.

executable_actions.on_failure: Stop at layer 1, do not build or verify the single-transformer layer, and route the failed evidence to Stage 8 failure localization with the failing leaf boundary and checker outputs.
executable_actions.rationale: Enforce the first repair-loop layer by proving every spatial operator leaf module before any single-layer merge or board wrapper work.

executable_actions.on_failure: Stop at layer 2, do not proceed to multilayer or board AXI/DDR verification, and send the single-layer boundary trace to Stage 8 for earliest-causal-boundary localization.
executable_actions.rationale: Execute the second repair-loop layer only after all leaf gates pass, validating the connected single transformer-layer kernel against golden/numeric and stream-order contracts.

executable_actions.on_failure: Stop before Vivado/backend/runtime bitstream, preserve tool logs and boundary traces, and route the earliest failing board AXI/DDR or pipeline boundary to Stage 8 bounded repair handoff.
executable_actions.rationale: Execute the third repair-loop layer by validating the multilayer pipeline, board AXI/DDR wrapper, protocol/order/address behavior, DDR roundtrip, deadlock watchdog, and real functional simulation before backend implementation.

executable_actions.on_failure: Keep the failed layer blocked; if localization or replay capability is insufficient, raise a checker/golden-reference repair request or stage_backtrack_request rather than claiming hardware correctness.
executable_actions.rationale: Any failed real-tool gate must be converted into a compact causal slice before repair; this prevents symptom patching and preserves the operator-leaf to single-layer to board-wrapper repair order.

executable_actions.on_failure: Block runtime bitstream and board runtime until target ambiguity is resolved with cited evidence or explicit bounded approval through backend recovery.
executable_actions.rationale: Backend/app-shell integration must derive target discovery policy from supplied board materials and real Stage 7/Vivado evidence; ambiguous shell targets require bounded approval rather than guessed names.

executable_actions.on_failure: Do not claim final hardware pass; route implementation, ABI, timing, or board-output failures to backend bounded recovery or Stage 8 localization using the failed checker evidence.
executable_actions.rationale: Vivado synthesis, implementation, runtime bitstream, ABI checks, and board runtime are downstream obligations and may run only after Stage 7 board AXI/DDR functional closure and target-discovery policy are accepted.

observations: state_summary.sacg_memory_truth reports zero active contamination barriers, zero open retry requests, and zero open backtrack requests; no current SACG-memory blocker is visible for Stage 6 promotion.

The candidate checker results show current-stage static/contract checks passing for verification_plan_static_check, tool_protocol_check, human_boundary_check, hierarchical_verification_plan_check, verification_artifact_contract_check, required_real_tool_evidence_check, and sacg_reference_check.

The role slice omits some detailed rows, but presence_summary asserts 9 stage agents, 6 merge agents, 13 debug boundaries, 22 evidence gates, 31 evidence-path requirements, 25 required tool protocols, and 31 verification-gate DAG nodes; missing-detail concerns should be handled by the final manifest/matrix handoff, not treated as a current-stage blocker.

The integrated DAG enforces bottom-up closure: leaf operator evidence precedes single-transformer-layer evidence; single-layer evidence precedes multilayer and board AXI/DDR wrapper evidence; functional simulation precedes Vivado/backend/runtime bitstream; board_runtime is last.

The maturity policy correctly prevents final pass claims while deadlock_watchdog, implementation_package_static, board_runtime, Vivado, runtime bitstream, and other real-tool evidence are pending downstream.

The debug_closure_contract contains the required bounded repair handoff fields: root_candidate_module, violated_contract, failure_signature, causal_path, targeted_replay_plan, and minimal_repair_context. Trace fields cover cycle, boundary_id, tx_id, tile_id, logical_index, observed_value, expected_value, contract, and status.
The contract forbids smoke-only acceptance and default generated weights as real-weight evidence; real input/weight artifacts and numeric/golden comparisons remain mandatory downstream gates.
No planned_tool or planned_checker gap is required by the visible evidence because all executable action tool roles and acceptance checkers used below are present in action_grounding_registry.
proposed_actions: Emit the final Stage 6 artifacts: final_verification_gate_dag.json, checker_evidence_acceptance_matrix.json, repair_boundary_handoff_contract.json, downstream_real_tool_execution_manifest.json, and stage6_promotion_decision.json.
Stage 7 must first materialize real input/weight manifests, DDR images, boundary contracts, and hashable testbench scaffolds before any functional acceptance run.
Execute Stage 7 layer 1 operator-leaf static, functional, golden, data-order, and transfer-count gates before any single-layer merge.
Execute Stage 7 layer 2 single-transformer-layer connection, functional, golden, numeric, and stream-order gates only after all leaf gates pass.
Execute Stage 7 layer 3 multilayer, deadlock, board-interface, AXI/DDR, protocol, DDR-roundtrip, and real functional-simulation gates before any Vivado/backend/runtime bitstream step.

Route any failed gate to Stage 8 contract-guided localization and bounded repair handoff using failure_localization_check, targeted_replay_check, causal_repair_context_check, and repair_boundary_check.

Keep backend_board actions downstream-only: app-shell target discovery and Vivado/runtime/board closure may proceed only after board AXI/DDR functional evidence is available and target evidence is unambiguous.
risks: Downstream, not current-stage blocking: the configured real tools have not yet produced leaf, single-layer, board AXI/DDR, Vivado, bitstream, or board-runtime evidence; failures must stop at the failed layer and enter the bounded repair loop.

Cross-layer consistency must be monitored during Stage 7 for Qwen2 GQA/RoPE/causal attention semantics, seq_len_bound 16, fp16/fp32 cast points, nearest-even rounding, lane/logical-index order, transfer counts, DDR address ranges, runtime ABI, and board target facts.

A higher-layer failure may challenge previously passed lower-layer evidence only when a contradicting boundary trace or CCTG-localized causal slice is produced; otherwise lower layers must not be reopened.

If a golden-reference, packer, checker, or testbench-scaffold capability fails to materialize, classify it as a checker/golden-reference or artifact-generation repair first, not as hardware correctness evidence.

Backend/app-shell target ambiguity remains a downstream risk; target names or shell integration points must be derived from supplied board materials and real Vivado/board evidence, or require bounded approval instead of guessing.
output.summary: Stage 6 evidence-gate audit passes as a verification plan/contract promotion only. The candidate declares the three required repair-loop layers, canonical checker/tool grounding is available in the registry, upstream Stage 3/4/5 static evidence is visible, sacg_memory_truth reports no active blockers, and downstream real-tool, Vivado, bitstream, and board-runtime evidence remain explicitly pending rather than claimed.
